question: Does sampling the unchanged selected baseline reveal an obvious TT access/contention cost concentration that would justify a bounded owner-gated investigation, rather than inferring a bottleneck from traffic counts?
purpose: Close T4's remaining cost-attribution question economically. Ordinary/hint probes and refresh counts establish traffic, not CPU cost. Sampling may be unable to resolve small/inlined costs; report that limit instead of treating absence as proof of zero cost.
scope: Read-only JDK21 JFR observation of ordinary default UCI BaselineEngine CP64 WIDEN16/flags262143/Hash64, diagnostics OFF. No TT/locking/layout/replacement/eligibility code or policy variant. No profiling result is strength evidence.
warmup: Two200k-node startpos requests per JVM, then ucinewgame per measured root. Full supplied real histories, deterministic corpus order. Warmup/startup are included in process/JFR lifetime but not request totals.
recording: Installed JDK21 profile.jfc settings, default sampling/monitor thresholds recorded verbatim from that file before execution. JFR dumponexit, separate native CPU, legal PV and exact whole-request node audit. Print only ExecutionSample, NativeMethodSample, JavaMonitorEnter and ThreadPark events into ignored raw JSON if available. No hidden threshold tuning after observation.
analysis: Preserve raw JFR and JSON, exact command/JVM/settings/runtime hashes and all requests. Count sampled stack presence by broad categories TT, Search, evaluation and other, noting overlapping inclusive categories. Report TT method frames and contended-monitor classes/durations if recorded. Default thresholds miss short waits; compiled/inlined attribution and finite sampling limit small-cost conclusions. Do not present sample share as an exact CPU percentage or causal savings estimate. Candidate clock outcomes play no role in profile selection.
decision: Only an obvious concentration supported by samples/contention evidence may motivate a bounded authority request with correctness/resource/verification alternatives. Otherwise retain duplicate probes/refreshes as unquantified micro-optimization opportunities; do not seek a TT redesign or launch a broad hot-path programme. No implementation of owner-reserved changes follows.
resources: Run after both adaptive clock domains have completed, before any further clock confirmation. One BelowNormal JVM at a time,1or4workers, Xms256m Xmx512m ActiveProcessorCount4. Estimated1-3min, each UCI request60s safety. Never overlap with clocks or other benchmarks; preserve failures and raw output. JFR overhead is intentionally unestimated, so do not use profiled timing as production performance.
